newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean shares close down as interest rates climb.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean shares close down as interest rates climb.

text.p: South Korean stocks ended lower on Monday under pressure from steadily climbing interest rates, brokers said.

They said investors were also worried that the Hanbo Steel loan scandal would flare up again due to demands from opposition politicians for further investigation into the role played by President Kim Young-sam's second son.
The stock index fell 4.65 points to a provisional close of 676.59, after hitting an intraday high of 686.94.
"The rising three-year corporate bond yields are the major reason for the decline," said Joo Whan of HG Asia Securities.
Joo said the trend would continue for the time being.

The benchmark three-year corporate bond yields were trading at 12.40 percent late Monday, slightly down from Saturday's 12.44 percent. But the rate was far higher than 12.02 percent seen early last week.
New corporate bonds are expected to skyrocket next month after applications were made for a record 3.91 trillion won worth of new issues for March.
Brokers said investors were also worried the central bank would tighten the money supply as the economic fallout of Hanbo's failure appeared to be subsiding.
The central bank had supplied trillions of won into the banking system to ease a financial squeeze after Hanbo Steel was declared insolvent on January 23.

Brokers said while investors did not have great expectations for President Kim's address to the parliament on Tuesday, there were hopes he would announce an early rise in the foreign shareholdings ceiling.
Earlier in the day, these hopes boosted market sentiment, especially in blue chips.
The ceiling is scheduled to be raised to 23 percent some time this year from the current 20 percent.

But opposition calls for further questioning of Kim's son, Hyun-chul, sparked fears "Hanbogate" was far from over. The younger Kim was cleared by prosecutors on Saturday of any wrongdoing in connection with the Hanbo scandal.

Samsung Electronics and Korea Mobile Telecom turned tail during the afternoon session. Samsung fell 500 won to 53,800, after touching a high of 55,700. Korea Mobile Telecom declined 15,000 won to 455,000, after reaching 489,500.
